tasks.short: Preview programmes and check transmission readiness

steps.what: Preview scheduled programs and verify signal functioning and transmission readiness

tasks.design: Retain audiovisual preview and signal checks using the {OTHER} broadcast monitoring system. Existing signal indicators support the technician without establishing that the correct programme is ready to transmit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readiness combines technical signals with recognition of the intended programme.
tasks.enabler_now: The supplied editing capabilities do not replace this preview judgment.
tasks.still_hard: Detecting wrong content or intermittent defects despite normal signal indicators.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise whether the actual programme and signal meet the transmission need.
tasks.altitude: Preview time and readiness assessment remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Separate signal presence from correct content

evidence.claim: Rough-cut editing capabilities do not establish replacement of broadcast signal preview.

assumptions: Boundary is preview and readiness assessment, excluding scheduling, live transmission and separate programme reporting.
Playout supplies the scheduled programme and monitoring equipment supplies signals; technician observes and judges during s1. No structured ready-for-transmission flag is assumed.
OTHER means broadcast monitoring system. Test native indicators before additions; no new automation is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no new system or workflow is introduced.
unknowns: Signal chain and current preview procedure
research_questions: Which readiness defects require direct programme preview rather than signal metrics?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100; gross and net zero. Recorded and live sources both retain readiness checks.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Design equipment changes against employer specifications and existing signal arrangements
Modify equipment and test its behaviour against the design and specifications

tasks.design: Retain engineering design in {DOCS} and physical modification and testing. No repeated drawing or parts-list baseline is presumed within this bespoke equipment task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Equipment changes depend on actual interfaces and operational constraints.
tasks.enabler_now: The supplied media editing capabilities do not establish replacement of engineering work.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising interactions between modified equipment and the existing signal chain.
tasks.human_edge: Make technically sound changes and verify actual operation.
tasks.altitude: Engineering and modification responsibility stay unchanged.

reach.learn: Express operational needs as testable technical constraints

evidence.claim: The digest supplies no demonstrated replacement for bespoke broadcast equipment design and physical modification.

assumptions: Boundary covers design and modification, excluding procurement and formal operational release processes.
Employer supplies requirements; technician examines documentation and actual equipment during s1 and s2. No structured compatible-or-safe flag is assumed.
Test existing engineering tools before additions; no new software or machine retrofit is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no new supporting workflow is introduced.
unknowns: Modification scope and technical approval arrangements
research_questions: Which requirements need physical measurement before design can be finalised?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives zero gross and net. Simple and complex changes retain design, physical work and testing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Review source material and define the intended broadcast edit
Assemble the first electronic edit from selected material

loop.purpose: Propose a script-matched rough timeline for speech-led material
loop.input: Verified edit brief, source recordings and generated timecoded transcript
loop.output: Rough timeline with source clip references
loop.check: Technician checks source audio/video, speaker meaning, edit context and continuity rather than trusting the transcript
loop.stop: One rough cut and one correction; mistranscribed, ambiguous or unsuitable footage returns to manual timeline assembly
loop.why_not_simpler: Native trims and presets are used first; matching spoken content across takes requires contextual reading

steps.what: Refine timing, check broadcast quality and accept the final edit

tasks.design: Use native editing presets in the {OTHER} media editing software before a bounded script-matching rough-cut feature. The technician checks actual source meaning and retains final timing, continuity and technical quality decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the specified spoken passages across takes requires repeated timeline work.
tasks.enabler_now: Transcript-based rough assembly can propose an editable first timeline.
tasks.still_hard: Preserving meaning and continuity across edits.
tasks.human_edge: Hear and see whether the edit communicates the intended material accurately.
tasks.altitude: Less rough assembly; final editing and technical acceptance remain human.

reach.learn: Recognise edits that change a speaker's meaning

evidence.claim: DaVinci Resolve IntelliScript matches transcripts to a script and builds a rough cut, rather than a finished edit.
This broadcast editing effort and savings scenario is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is editing and internal acceptance, excluding publication and live transmission.

Technician captures job/version, source clip ids, intended passages, script version, duration and editorial constraints in s1. Capture retains30%; incomplete instructions require manual clarification.

Editing software produces the timecoded transcript from source recordings within s2; transcript checking and source listening are included in its26 retained hours. Missing or unreliable transcript segments are manually assembled, never treated as absent speech.
OTHER means media editing software. Test native trimming, presets and script tools first. Scenario applies to speech-led rough assembly; music-led or bespoke visual editing may remain manual.
unknowns: Material mix, script quality and existing editing features
research_questions: Does checked rough assembly reduce total editing time without meaning-changing cuts?

already_counted.description: Source review and edit brief capture
Transcript and rough-cut review plus final editing and acceptance

incremental.description: Maintain presets and inspect recurring transcription or matching errors
Maintain media access and editing environment

approvals.approved_version: Exact timeline, source versions, audio mix and final export settings; changes void internal acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R86 gives14 gross minus8 upkeep=6 net. Non-speech or already assisted edits yield zero; repeated script-led rough assembly may yield2%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Organise recording sessions and prepare recording areas

steps.what: Agree recording requirements, participant availability and booth or station needs
Prepare session schedules and recording setup lists
Check the session plan, confirm arrangements and prepare recording areas and equipment
outputs: confirmed session and prepared recording area

tasks.design: Use native {CALENDAR} booking views and {DOCS} setup templates to prepare a draft plan. The technician confirms arrangements and retains physical booth preparation, routing and setup checks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreed requirements are copied into schedules and setup lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Native booking and template features can generate the repeated plan structure.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising physical room or equipment problems before recording.
tasks.human_edge: Coordinate participants and prepare the actual recording environment.
tasks.altitude: Less plan assembly; physical setup and coordination remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Translate agreed requirements into practical setup checks

evidence.claim: Configured recording schedules and setup lists are a model knowledge proposal, not a measured digest case.

assumptions: Boundary includes session organisation and area preparation, excluding performance and separate production editing.

Technician captures session id, confirmed participants, availability, duration, room, equipment requirements and setup checklist version in s1. Obtaining responses and capture are retained; missing availability or equipment status requires manual confirmation.
Participants and equipment custodians provide existing responses; four other-role incremental hours below cover extra structured entry and support. No free ready-room flag is assumed.
Test native CALENDAR resource booking and DOCS templates first; existing automatic schedule generation yields no additional saving.
unknowns: Current booking setup and repeated plan entry effort
research_questions: Can native session plans reduce repeated entry without increasing setup omissions?

already_counted.description: Requirement clarification, availability confirmation and capture
Plan check, arrangement confirmation and physical preparation

incremental.description: Maintain setup templates and resolve booking exceptions
Additional structured updates and configuration support

approvals.approved_version: Exact session, confirmed time, participants, room and setup list; changes require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R80 gives20 gross minus6 upkeep=14 net. Existing booking templates yield zero; repeated manual plan assembly may yield3%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Some rough editing and session plan assembly gain support; signal preview, engineering and physical setup remain human.
reach: Coordinate edit meaning and setup requirements with editors and sound technicians
role.ambitious_version: A broadcast technician who reuses accurate plans and rough edits while retaining direct technical oversight.
